 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports the Thunder have agreed on a two-way contract with Micah Peavy. 
 Peavy was waived by the Grizzlies earlier this week and went unclaimed. Now the former 18th overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft will try to carve out a role for himself on the Thunder. He reportedly picked Oklahoma City over Toronto as the Raptors had also offered him a two-way contract. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Walter Clayton 
 FA 
 Guard 
 #4 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Grizzlies waived Walter Clayton Jr. and Micah Peavy. 
 The 18th overall pick in the 2025 draft, Clayton was traded from Utah to Memphis as part of the Jaren Jackson Jr. deal in February. Even with the Grizzlies’ point guard rotation in flux due to injuries and a desire to trade Ja Morant, Clayton couldn’t carve out a consistent role in Memphis. Earlier Monday, the Grizzlies reportedly hoped to trade WCJ, but they couldn’t make a deal happen. As for Peavy, the Grizzlies acquired him from the Pelicans in the summer along with Jordan Hawkins, who was waived earlier in the preseason. 
 Micah Peavy 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 Micah Peavy (ankle) will not be available when the Grizzlies open training camp on Tuesday. 
 Acquired from the Pelicans in early September, Peavy recently sprained his ankle. According to Grizzlies GM Zach Kleiman, it will be “a while” before the team gets to see the 2025 second-round pick on the court. Peavy’s absence won’t affect fantasy basketball, but it does mean one less wing competing for rotation minutes when camp opens. 
 Micah Peavy 
 MEM 
 Guard-Forward 
 #14 
 The Pelicans traded Micah Peavy, Jordan Hawkins, a future second-round pick and a second-round pick swap to the Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson. 
 The 40th overall pick in the 2025 draft, Peavy averaged 15.0 minutes per game across 61 appearances for the Pelicans as a rookie. He averaged 4.3 points per game in those appearances, shooting 38.5 percent from the field. With the Grizzlies rebuilding, there may be opportunities for Peavy to contribute, but he’s unlikely to be a consistent actor in fantasy basketball next season. 
 Micah Peavy 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #14 
 Micah Peavy contributed 16 points (6-of-11 FGs), three rebounds, five assists, two steals and two three-pointers on Thursday against the Timberwolves. 
 The lone pick from the Pelicans 2025 class that suited up for summer league, Peavy was one of the best players on the floor for New Orleans in this game. Peavy was an effective defender as a rookie, so seeing him produce on offense is encouraging, even if he has a long way to go to crack the Pelicans’ rotation this season. 
 Micah Peavy 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #14 
 Micah Peavy accounted for 21 points (6-of-12 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Timberwolves. 
 A 20-point scorer in two of his last three games, Peavy finished Sunday’s defeat with a new season-high in points. The rookie wing shot 50 percent from the field and recorded a complete stat line, taking advantage of the extended minutes. While Peavy’s redraft league value for next season will remain extremely low due to the Pelicans’ wing depth, he’ll be worth taking a flier on in dynasty leagues. 
 Saddiq Bey 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #41 
 Saddiq Bey (rest) is questionable for Friday’s game against the Celtics. 
 While Bey was not on the Pelicans’ injury report for Tuesday’s win over the Jazz, the Pelicans decided not to play him. Micah Peavy moved into the starting lineup and had the best offensive showing of his rookie season. Look for him to play heavy minutes again if Bey isn’t available. 
 Micah Peavy 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #14 
 Micah Peavy amassed 20 points (9-of-13 FGs), four rebounds, two assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Jazz. 
 Peavy has not been a consistent member of the Pelicans’ rotation this season, which makes this part of the season that much more important for him. The 20 points were a season-high for the rookie wing, who finished a blocked shot shy of a complete stat line. Peavy’s contract for the 2025-26 season is guaranteed, so he is secure in that regard. The goal now is to solidify a spot in the rotation for himself. 
 Derik Queen 
 NOP 
 Center 
 #22 
 Jeremiah Fears, Jordan Poole, Micah Peavy, Derik Queen and Kevon Looney will start Tuesday’s game against the Jazz. 
 Herb Jones, Saddiq Bey and Zion Williamson are active for Tuesday’s game, but none are expected to play according to interim head coach James Borrego. Fears is the lone holdover from the lineup that started Sunday’s loss to the Magic, with Poole, Peavy, Queen and Looney all starting. 
 Saddiq Bey 
 NOP 
 Guard-Forward 
 #41 
 According to Pelicans interim head coach James Borrego, Saddiq Bey will be active for Tuesday’s game against the Jazz but is not expected to play. 
 Bey is absent from the Pelicans’ injury report, which makes this a bad situation for fantasy managers in active leagues. Micah Peavy should play extended minutes, especially with Herb Jones and Zion Williamson also not expected to play. Like Bey, Jones and Williamson are not on the injury report.

 Bryce McGowens (toe) is out for Wednesday’s game against the Raptors. 
 McGowens has a fractured small toe on his right foot, which may keep him out of multiple games. There may be additional minutes for Micah Peavy, but not enough to affect fantasy basketball.
